definition: Learning models or representations with many zero components — sparse coding, sparsity-regularized networks — for efficiency and interpretability.
details: Learning models or representations with many zero components — sparse coding, sparsity-regularized networks — for efficiency and interpretability.

explainer.lead: Sparse learning builds models or representations with many zero components, via sparse coding or sparsity-regularised networks. It matters for both efficiency and interpretability.

tiers.eli5: It is like packing light: the model deliberately keeps most of its parts switched off so only a few matter for any given answer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add sparsity regularisation or use sparse coding to shrink active components. The pitfall is over-regularising and dropping signal the model needed.
tiers.paperLevel: Learning models or representations with many zero components—sparse coding and sparsity-regularised networks—for efficiency and interpretability.

explainer.example: A network trained with a sparsity penalty ends up with most weights at zero, leaving a smaller set of active connections that is easier to inspect.
